title: Agents for Experiments, Experiments for Agents: A Design Grammar for AI-Enabled Experimental Science
abstract: arXiv:2605.17746v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Human-AI experiments vary who receives information, who can act, and who holds decision authority. Precise descriptions of individual studies do not by themselves provide a common language for comparing these arrangements. This conceptual commentary proposes SEED (Structural Encoding for Experimental Discovery), a grammar that represents each experimental condition as a typed actor-flow graph. Its purpose is to organize publicly documented studies into a shared library of consistently represented conditions. Human researchers and AI systems can use this common reference to understand prior arrangements and propose extensions for new research questions. The grammar distinguishes structural changes from attribute variation; the scientific value of a proposed change requires substantive argument and evidence. translated_title: 用于实验的智能体，用于智能体的实验：AI赋能实验科学的设计语法
translated_abstract: 人类与AI实验在信息接收者、行动执行者以及决策权归属上各不相同。对单个研究的精确描述本身并不能为比较这些安排提供一种共同语言。本概念性评述提出了SEED（Structural Encoding for Experimental Discovery，实验发现的结构化编码），这是一种将每个实验条件表示为类型化“行动者—信息流”图的语法。其目的是将公开记录的研究组织成一个由一致表示的条件构成的共享库。人类研究者与AI系统可以利用这一共同参照来理解先前的实验安排，并针对新的研究问题提出扩展方案。该语法区分了结构性变化与属性变化；一项被提出的改动要具有科学价值，仍需有实质性的论证和证据支持。计算示例展示了SEED如何支持实验设计的比较以及AI辅助的候选实验开发。
tldr: 本文提出了SEED语法，将实验条件表示为类型化的行动者—信息流图，为人机实验设计建立了共同语言，使人类研究者和AI系统能够系统地比较已有实验安排并协作开发新的实验方案。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes SEED, a grammar that represents experimental conditions as typed actor-flow graphs, establishing a common language for human-AI experimental design that enables researchers and AI systems to systematically compare prior arrangements and collaboratively develop new experiments.
